name: OpenQM
tagline: Compact MultiValue (Pick) database from Ladybridge, once GPL-licensed, now Rocket's entry-level MV product.
description: OpenQM is a MultiValue database written by Martin Phillips at Ladybridge Systems in the UK, designed as a lean, modern implementation of the Pick model with QMBasic, a query language and good compatibility with other Pick dialects. For a period an open-source GPL edition was published, which later seeded the community fork ScarletDME; the main product remained commercial. Zumasys acquired OpenQM in 2019 and it passed to Rocket Software with the Zumasys portfolio in 2021, where it now sits as Rocket Open QM alongside UniVerse, UniData and jBASE. It is a reasonable low-cost home for small Pick applications, with a very small community.

pricing.notes: Commercial per-user licences; a free personal/evaluation licence has been offered.

strengths: Small, efficient implementation of the Pick MultiValue model
Good compatibility with other Pick dialects eases migration
QMClient API reachable from Python and other languages
Low entry cost compared with larger MV platforms
weaknesses: Tiny community and sparse public release information
Overlaps with Rocket's other MV products, so long-term focus is uncertain
No replication or scaling features of note
useCases: Migrating off ageing Pick systems to commodity servers
